content: We compare two types of subwords: simple n-grams (like fastText) and unsupervised morphemes. For example, given the word “cat”, we mark beginning and end with angled brackets and use all n-grams of length 3 to 6 as subwords, yielding $S_{\textnormal {cat}} = \lbrace  \textnormal {$ $ ca, at$ $, cat} \rbrace $ . Morfessor BIBREF11 is used to probabilistically segment words into morphemes. The Morfessor model is trained using raw text so it is entirely unsupervised. For the word “subsequent”, we get $S_{\textnormal {subsequent}} = \lbrace  \textnormal {$ $ sub, sequent$ $} \rbrace $ .
